spec.description: Alerts issued over roughly the last seven days, whether or not they are still in effect, newest first, optionally narrowed. For only what is in effect now, use `alerts.get_active_alerts`.

request.title: ListAlertsRequest
request.description: How to narrow the alerts. Every filter is optional; the array-valued ones are sent as repeated query keys and mean "any of". `area`, `point`, `region`, `region_type` and `zone` exclude each other: send at most one.

start.description: Earliest `sent` time to include. The service keeps about the last seven days of alerts.

status.description: Alert statuses to include. Lower-case, unlike every other enumerated filter here. Pass `actual` to leave out drills and tests.

message_type.description: Message types to include: a new alert, an update to one, or its cancellation.

event.description: Event names to include, such as `Red Flag Warning`.

code.description: Three-letter event codes to include, such as `SVR` (severe thunderstorm warning).

area.description: Two-letter state, territory or marine-area codes to narrow to, such as `WA` or `PZ`. Sent as a repeated query key. Left un-enumerated deliberately: the service's own 400 lists only the marine half of what it accepts, and a guessed enum would reject the states.

point.description: A `latitude,longitude` pair; returns the alerts covering that point.

items.description: One marine region: `AL` Alaska, `AT` Atlantic, `GL` Great Lakes, `GM` Gulf of Mexico, `PA` Pacific, `PI` Pacific Islands.

region_type.description: Only land or only marine alerts.

limit.description: Most alerts to return. Range [1, 500]; defaults to 500.

cursor.description: Opaque page cursor. Use a standard URL parser to percent-decode the `cursor` query value from the previous response's `pagination.next` URL, and resend the original filters and limit. Stop on an empty page or absent next cursor; a short non-empty page can still have a next page.

response.description: The alerts, as a GeoJSON feature collection with a `pagination.next` link.

notes: No `pagination` block: `pagination.next` is a whole URL, and the token strategy cannot extract its query value. Use a standard URL parser (Python: parse_qs(urlsplit(next_url).query); TypeScript: new URL(nextUrl).searchParams; Rust: Url::query_pairs) to percent-decode the cursor exactly once. Resend every original filter and limit with that cursor: the next URL can omit them. Stop on an empty page or absent next cursor, never merely a short non-empty page. Python review measured 100 rows, then 76 with a next link, then empty.

A `seek` walk over `start`/`end` is plausible but undeclared. The window bounds `sent` and the service answers newest first by it (measured 2026-09-30: all 177 actual alerts of 00:00 to 06:00Z on 2026-09-29 were sent inside the window, in descending order), but `sent` repeats (two alerts at 05:57Z in the first five rows), so the walk would need `unique: false`, and its anchor has not been measured.
The deprecated `active` flag is left out; the OpenAPI marks it deprecated and points at `alerts.get_active_alerts`.
Enumerations are the ones `alerts.get_active_alerts` copied from the service's 400 replies; `message_type` and `region_type` are the OpenAPI's.
